title: Unit 56 rem early
english: He brought lions upon them—not dragons, not the other great beasts, but gnats and dog-flies, upon frog and locust.
What is 'he drowned'?—but there he does not say:
'I have mocked them' (Ex 10:2).
'The sinners drew the sword and bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy' (Ps 36:14).
They prepared a sword, that they might cast down the poor and needy.
It is turned back and comes into their own heart, as it is said:
'he who digs a pit for his neighbor shall fall into it' (Prov 26:27).
And again:
'and let the trap which they hid catch them' (Ps 34:8).
And in Ecclesiastes he says:
'him who destroys a hedge, a serpent shall bite' (Eccl 10:8).
A serpent shall bite the one destroying another's hedge, destroying another's security.
'They drew the sword';
they drew it from the sheath into the open [...].
The sword can be the word with guile;
for they draw it, that through it they may strike.
You have it said in Proverbs:
'there are those who, speaking, wound as with a sword, but the tongues of the wise heal' (Prov 12:18).
There are those who in speaking wound as with a sword.
But it is to be read with the dative:
there are those who in speaking wound with a sword.
Those who corrupt good manners with evil conversations (1 Cor 15:33) wound with a sword in speaking.
'and their tongue is a sharp sword';
their word, like a sword, harms and wounds.
In speaking, then, there are some who wound with a sword; but the tongues of the wise, the words of the wise, heal.
These swords are of medicine; they do not wound, do not strike, do not traumatize, but heal the wounds made by other words.
A bow being bent is the ruling faculty thus prepared so that arrows are loosed from it.
And let these be evil reasonings, harmful words.
'behold, the sinners bent the bow, they prepared arrows for the quiver'.
'to slay the upright in heart' (Ps 36:14).
Here we hear 'upright in heart' as the righteous one being reproved, and the wise, and the righteous one accusing himself.
In the Gospel it is written in the person of the Lord that:
'all who take the sword shall perish by the sword' (Matt 26:52).
And the many think that this says that everyone who slays a man shall be slain.
But this does not appear incontrovertible;
many murderers have met their own end;
but this is what it says:

everyone who brings punishment upon someone shall fall under punishment; everyone wishing to harm someone with a sword—with his own sharpened mind, or tongue and word—shall fall under the same things.
'to cast down the poor and needy' (Ps 36:14)?—they cannot cast down the rich; they cannot cast down the one having the 'in all knowledge and all word' (1 Cor 1:5) wealth, but the [...].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Famine of the Word and the Vanishing of Sinners
english: A poor and needy person, even if the heart seems straight, as previously said, like the one being reproved who is wise and the accuser who is righteous of himself; but rather the sword, turned against those who have become blunt, strikes and destroys them; likewise the bow is broken. And it is well to say: 'Let their sword enter into their heart.' This sword, which is harmful, the one of the enemies is not continuous [text gapped] and in days of famine they shall be satisfied [text gapped] of those feeding the soul, those watering it.

In the prophet, indeed, it is said, where it is written: 'I will bring a famine upon the earth, not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord' (Amos 8:11), it is applied: 'Many have fallen in every place, I will cast down silence' (Psalm 142:6). To the fallen, the famine is. To these, however, the silence of the divine word is brought. Thus, 'in days of famine they shall be satisfied.' Because the sinners shall perish.

Twice again we perceive the destruction of the sinners: namely, in the way they are sinners, they perish having experienced the oppressors. The righteous 'are not ashamed in evil time' (2 Timothy 2:15), but the sinners are ashamed. When they are ashamed, knowing how evil they are, and they blush because of sinning, sometimes they despise the sin and become free from it, and thus they perish in such a way that they are no longer sinners.

But the enemies of the Lord, at the same time as they are to be glorified and exalted, having vanished like smoke, they vanished. Sinners are able to be enemies of the Lord. And it is possible also to call sinners those who sin according to ethics, those who transgress the divine commandments, and enemies of the Lord those who think impiously, those outside godliness, those who falsely glorify. These, therefore, are the enemies of the Lord, who at the same time as being to be glorified and exalted immediately vanished like smoke. And behold, always he likens sinners to smoke. And in another psalm it is said: 'As smoke vanishes, so they vanished; as wax melts from before the fire, so the sinners shall perish from before the face of God' (Psalm 68:2).

The word constructs the argument, that the sinners are not of another nature. The smoke is a follower of fire, and the wax of honey. And previously the honey takes origin. Since it does not consist otherwise than in wax, the wax by habit consists. Not because of the wax the honey, but because of the honey the wax, and not because of the smoke the fire, but because of the fire the smoke. The sinners, therefore, according to the smoke, vanish having a following; for sinning itself and enmity toward [the Lord]...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Follower of Virtue and the Loan of God
english: Sin is a follower of virtue. The rational animal has become capable of virtue. Yet this capability is not an essence of any kind. Humans are not good by essence; for they were created so that they might become good through participation in the truly good. But the capacity for evil follows the capacity for virtue. Just as the bad always follows the good, bad art follows art, and mishearing follows hearing. Sin, therefore, is a follower of virtue; the sinning animal would not exist if it were not capable of virtue.

Similarly, wax is a follower. For this [substance] does not turn into non-existence, but changes into something better. And sinners become smoke because of this very evil; for lawlessness is in a certain way like a harmful eye or smoke to the eyes. You see that lawlessness becomes to those using it like smoke to the eyes. Smoke does not need great force to be overturned, for it is quickly overturned. Therefore, sinners are 'as wax melts from the presence of fire,' and 'as smoke vanishes, so let them vanish.' Smoke is, as I have said, a follower of fire; for it exists because fire exists or comes to be.

Thus the enemies of the Lord, even if they blaze brightly and are praised as capable or promising, are extinguished like smoke at the very moment they are exalted. It is ours to see their vanishing; for even if they remain for a time, being glorified and praised and thinking great things, those able to see that which they think great find them instantly vanishing. 'The borrower does not repay' (Psalm 36:28).

What God gives for the benefit of humans and the soul, those receiving do not take as a debt; for no one receives anything in this age as a debt, but giving as a gift, the good man gives a loan so that, having worked with it, he may gain and give interest. I take the word concerning righteousness. If I give back and also provide interest, I offer the works of righteousness to God. But if, having received the word concerning righteousness, I do nothing according to righteousness, having borrowed from God, I have not repaid; for God gives so that we may act, and God provides so that we may turn words into deeds. His divine silver is lent, concerning which it is said, 'silver refined is a test for the earth' (Psalm 66:3). The borrower therefore pays back interest and also that which he received. But the righteous man shows mercy and gives.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
